title: GitHub Actions tampering
overview: Review a workflow file change that broadened job permissions without corresponding protection or review.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and github organization audit projection fields.

attack.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
attack.rationale: A risky workflow edit can set up poisoned pipeline execution. The fixture records a configuration change without executing a job.

hypothesis: A workflow update that adds write permissions outside approved review warrants examining the diff and executed jobs.
evidence: Use the changed path, permissions delta and review status. Pivot to revision, branch rules and any resulting run.
false_positive: An emergency policy adjustment can add scoped write rights before normal release workflows run.
tuning: Require independently recorded emergency approval and expiration. Inspect permissions by individual job.
response: Preserve the diff, inspect runner and job logs, revert an unauthorized workflow change and scope token exposure.
prevention: Protect workflow paths with CODEOWNERS and required review. Set least-privilege and explicit workflow permissions.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: Changed paths and permission deltas come from a synthetic GitHub audit and diff join. A push alone does not show workflow execution.

questions.prompt: What changed the risk of the workflow?
questions.explanation: A Git metadata change matters here because it expanded what jobs could do.

questions.prompt: What should you inspect after preserving the diff?
options: The run and downstream actions, if any
questions.explanation: The resulting workflow runs determine whether the expanded permission was used.
